While it may not be feasible to visually inspect these components, their proper functioning can be verified by leveling the build platform, moving platforms freely, removing obstructing powder, and cleaning or replacing felt seals. The facility's cleanliness and organization also play a critical role in maintaining machine health. The room should be regularly cleaned to prevent cross-contamination, ensure operator safety, and provide adequate working space to move machinery and powder containers without obstruction. Floors, shelves, and tables should be kept clean to prevent slippery surfaces and fine powder buildup, which can pose a safety hazard. Operator training is another crucial aspect, as it ensures consistency and repeatability in powder handling, program setup, machine setup, cleaning, and part break-out procedures. Operators should receive training from vendor facilities, on-site vendor-trained engineers, or primary operators to ensure a uniform standard of operation. It's essential to recognize that each machine may require unique care and attention, which can be determined by regular operators or for special cases. 1.3.1 Part-Part Production Variability In AM, parts are prone to variations both within a build and between builds, due to deviations that can occur along the build platform. These deviations can arise from various factors, including inconsistent powder layer deposition, non-uniform airflow, differences in laser beam intensity at different locations, powder characteristics, and asymmetrical part geometry. As a result, it is essential to consider all major aspects of the AM process, including material selection, data preparation, and process parameters, before fabrication. Each of these factors can significantly impact the variability of parts, and therefore, must be carefully evaluated and controlled to ensure consistent and high-quality output. The quality of the fabricated component is heavily influenced by the raw materials used, which is why regular characterization of the powders' composition and behavior is crucial. In the data preparation stage, component designs, models, and simulations are created to ensure optimal fabrication orientation, identify potential defects, and determine the need for support structures. The design is then reviewed, and any features that may lead to defects are redesigned. Upon finalizing the design, the sliced model is generated in the proper format for the system, and simulation software is used to analyze the model, identify fabrication risks, predict part distortion, and estimate shrinkage compensation factors to achieve accurate geometries. This step can help optimize the building process and reduce production time. After review and simulations, the part must be properly oriented to prevent recoating issues that could damage or impact the completion of the part. The process parameters, which rely on laser stability and adequate energy density, are critical in achieving full density parts.
